tagline: Petronas Twin Towers over a street-food city — Batu Caves' rainbow stairs, the night markets of Jalan Alor and three cultures layered into one skyline.
overview: Kuala Lumpur mixes Malay, Chinese and Indian worlds in a single skyline crowned by the Petronas Twin Towers — the tallest twin buildings on earth, joined by a skybridge on the 41st floor.

The city's soul is at street level: Jalan Alor's nightly food market, the red lanterns of Petaling Street, and the colonial-era Sultan Abdul Samad buildings at Merdeka Square, where independence was declared in 1957.

Fifteen minutes north, Batu Caves' 272 rainbow steps climb to Hindu temples inside a limestone cave, guarded by a 43-metre golden Murugan and a troupe of monkeys. Speed's 2024 tour stop drew some of the biggest crowds of the whole trip.

funFacts.title: THE TALLEST TWINS
funFacts.text: The Petronas Towers were the world's tallest buildings 1998–2004 — still the tallest twins.

funFacts.title: RAINBOW STAIRS
funFacts.text: Batu Caves' 272 rainbow-painted steps became an instant icon in 2018.

funFacts.title: THREE CULTURES, ONE CITY
funFacts.text: Mosques, Hindu temples and Chinese clan houses sit streets apart.

funFacts.title: A NIGHTLY FOOD COURT
funFacts.text: Jalan Alor packs about 200 stalls of satay, noodles and durian every night.

funFacts.title: MERDEKA SQUARE
funFacts.text: Independence was proclaimed here in 1957 — the flagpole is among the world's tallest.

funFacts.title: A MUDDY NAME
funFacts.text: 'Kuala Lumpur' means 'muddy confluence' — two muddy rivers built a metropolis.

funFacts.title: FIREFLIES NEARBY
funFacts.text: Kuala Selangor's firefly colonies glow an hour from the towers.

funFacts.title: RAINFOREST INSIDE
funFacts.text: KL Forest Eco Park keeps primary rainforest in the city centre.

funFacts.title: MONKEY USHERS
funFacts.text: Batu Caves' macaques escort — and rob — pilgrims climbing the stairs.

funFacts.title: THE CROSSROADS
funFacts.text: KL sits midway between Singapore and Bangkok, Southeast Asia's natural hub.

faq.a: Kuala Lumpur is in Malaysia, in Asia.

faq.q: What is the population of Kuala Lumpur?
faq.a: The greater Kuala Lumpur area is home to about 8,800,000 people.

faq.q: What is Kuala Lumpur famous for?
faq.a: Kuala Lumpur is famous for the Petronas Twin Towers, Batu Caves' rainbow steps and the Jalan Alor night food market.
